title: A Method to Achieve Transient and Reversible Optical Transparency in Live Animals via the Kramers-Kronig Relations
content: Optical imaging and stimulation are crucial techniques for visualizing and modulating the structure and function of biological tissues. However, the inherent scattering of light within biological tissues poses a significant challenge, hindering noninvasive deep-tissue optical imaging in live animals. In this talk, I will introduce a novel approach to engineering the scattering properties of biological tissues using the Kramers-Kronig relations, thereby achieving optical transparency in a transient and reversible manner in live animals. This method has allowed us to visualize deep-seated structures and functions through optically transparent tissues in live mice, with the potential to enable noninvasive deep-brain imaging and optogenetics.
